title: Real-world class and object example
answer: A class can be compared to a real-world product definition, while an object is one concrete item described by that definition. In AeroTopo, `Orthomosaic` is the class: it defines an identifier, source tile collection, ground-sample-distance field, validation, and resolution behavior. An object such as `new Orthomosaic("ORTHO-2026", tiles, 0.05)` is one specific orthomosaic product with its own values. Another Orthomosaic object can use a different id, tiles, and resolution while sharing the same class behavior.
